Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.2. Wholesome States of the Fine-Material Sphere (Rūpāvacara-kusala) 2.1.2.1.
The Method of Fourfold Categories (Catukkanaya) Which phenomena are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states,
and enters and dwells in the first jhāna— accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, and filled with rapture and pleasure—
taking the earth-kasiṇa as its object, at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on].
These states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, there is internal serenity...

With the one-pointedness of mind, free from applied thought and sustained thought, born of concentration, accompanied by rapture and pleasure, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa.
At that time, there is contact; there is feeling; there is perception; there is volition; there is consciousness;
there is rapture; there is pleasure; there is one-pointedness of mind; there is the faculty of faith.
There is the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration,
the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental pleasure, and the faculty of life. There is right view,
right effort … [and so on] … there is exertion, and there is non-distraction.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial states exist at that time—these states are wholesome ...
[as before] ... At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments; there are eight faculties; there is a three-factored jhāna; there is a four-factored path;
there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena;
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [as before] ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right effort …pe… exertion, non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial states exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception,
and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These phenomena are wholesome.
Which phenomena are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, and through the fading away of rapture, one dwells in equanimity—
Mindful and clearly comprehending, he experiences pleasure with the body, of which the Noble Ones declare:
“He dwells in happiness, mindful and equanimous”; thus he enters and dwells in the third jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa.
At that time, there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, and there is pleasure.
There is one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration,
the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental pleasure, the faculty of vitality, right view,
right effort …pe… there is exertion, and there is non-distraction.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [and so on] ...
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments; there are eight faculties; there is two-factored jhāna; there is the four-factored path;
there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena;
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [as before] ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right effort …pe… exertion, non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception,
and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the realm of form, through the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain...

With the previous disappearance of both joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and possesses purity of mindfulness through equanimity, with the earth-kasiṇa as his object. At that time, there is contact,
there is feeling, there is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind, and there is the faculty of faith.
There is the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration,
the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of life, right view,
right effort … [and so on] … exertion, and non-distraction.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome … [as before] … At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments; there are eight faculties; there is two-factored jhāna; there is the four-factored path;
there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena;
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [as before] ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right effort …pe… exertion, non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception,
and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, is the aggregate of formations …pe…
These states are wholesome.

at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before].
These phenomena are wholesome.
Which phenomena are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm—without applied thought, with sustained thought only, born of concentration, accompanied by rapture and pleasure—
Having attained and dwelling in the second jhāna with the earth-kasiṇa, at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is sustained thought, there is rapture, there is pleasure,
there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of faith, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of mindfulness, there is the faculty of concentration.
There is the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental pleasure,
the faculty of vital energy, right view, right effort … [and so on] … there is exertion,
there is non-distraction; or whatever other dependent-originated, formless states exist at that time.
These states are wholesome ...
[and so on] ... At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three nutriments, eight faculties, a fourfold jhāna, and a fourfold path.
There is [the mind], there are seven powers, there are three roots, there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena,
there is one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial states exist at that time.
These states are wholesome ...
[as before] ... What, at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of vitality, right view, right effort ... [as before] ... exertion, non-distraction.
Or whatever other conditioned, formless phenomena exist at that time, excluding the feeling aggregate, excluding the perception aggregate,
and excluding the consciousness aggregate— this, at that time, is the formations aggregate …pe… these phenomena are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought,
one enters and dwells in the third jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, and so forth.
There is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is rapture, there is pleasure, there is one-pointedness of mind,
there is the faculty of faith, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of mindfulness, there is the faculty of concentration,
there is the faculty of wisdom, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of mental joy, there is the faculty of vital energy, and there is right view.
There is right effort … there is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are wholesome … [and so on] ….”
At that time, there are four aggregates; there are two bases; there are two elements;
there are three nutriments; there are eight faculties; there is a jhāna with three factors; there is a path with four factors;
there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one mental-object base.
There is the element of mental objects;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [and so on].
What on that occasion is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right effort …pe… exertion, non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial states there are on that occasion, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness.
At that time, this is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) … [as before] … These phenomena are wholesome (kusala).
What phenomena are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm, through the fading away of rapture … [and so on] … enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna with the earth-kasiṇa,
at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is pleasure, there is one-pointedness of mind, and there is the faculty of faith.
There is the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration,
the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind, the faculty of mental pleasure, the faculty of life, right view,
right effort …pe… there is exertion, and there is non-distraction.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome … [as before] … At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, eight faculties, two-factored jhāna, four-factored path,
seven powers, three roots, one contact …pe… one base of mental phenomena,
one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are wholesome ... [as before] ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, right view, right effort …pe… exertion, non-distraction;
or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception,
and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These states are wholesome.

At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the realm of form, with the abandoning of pleasure … [and so on] … these states are wholesome.
He enters and dwells in the fifth jhāna based on the earth-kasiṇa. At that time, there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is equanimity, there is one-pointedness of mind,
there is the faculty of faith, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of mindfulness, there is the faculty of concentration, and there is the faculty of wisdom.
There is the mind faculty, there is the equanimity faculty, there is the life faculty, there is right view,
there is right effort …pe… there is exertion, there is non-distraction; or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time.

[and so on] ... At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three nutriments, eight faculties, a two-factored jhāna, and a four-factored path.
there is [the mind]; there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena (*dhammāyatana*);

or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are wholesome ... [as above] ...

[and so forth] ...one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is immeasurable, has a limited object, and consists of the earth-kasiṇa; at that time there is contact...
[and so forth] ...there is non-distraction... [and so forth].

He enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna …pe… the first jhāna …pe… he enters and dwells in the fifth jhāna, limited with a limited object, the earth-kasiṇa …pe…

at that time there is contact … non-distraction … [and so on] … there is non-distraction.

At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm—being percipient of the formless internally, seeing forms externally as limited, and having mastered them with the thought "I know, I see"—and thus, secluded from sensual pleasures, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, at that time there is contact... and so on... there is non-distraction... and so on.
These phenomena are wholesome.
Which phenomena are wholesome?

Having overcome those limited [perceptions], "I know, I see"—with the stilling of applied and sustained thought... the second jhāna...
the third jhāna...
the fourth jhāna... [and so forth].
